text: ML Drift's AppleInfo constructor matches the lowercased Metal device name against a fixed table of names ('apple a7' ... 'apple a20 pro', 'apple m1' ... 'apple m6') by substring, keeping the longest matching key; a name with no match leaves gpu_type = AppleGpu::kUnknown and GetGpuFamily returns Family::kApple1. In our build (ours: e5e4c6eb), CreateGpuInfoFromMetalDevice then gives an Apple GPU of unknown type the highest Apple family its MTLDevice supports (supportsFamily, Apple10 down to Apple2, else Apple1) and an estimated compute-unit count, 6 on iOS and 10 on macOS; a known name's family still comes only from the name.
